proposedOverrides.summary: Localized Late Chulmun archaeology with atlas defects disclosed.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact target id is koreans, display name Koreans, circa 2000 to 1500 BCE; the label and imported modern ethnicity summary are anachronistic for the archaeological interval.
The lone exact geometry has seventeen components and 652 positions, extends across much of northern and eastern China, includes Jilin and Shenyang, and omits sampled northeastern peninsula points.
A direct encoded arc shared with the thai layer is a map construction defect, not an ancient cultural border.
Claims are localized to named Korean Peninsula sites and separate direct finds, laboratory measurements, models, and clearly labeled comparison.
Chulmun is a material-culture period label, not one people, language, state, ethnicity, or uniform economy.
No contemporaneous writing is securely attributable; later Chinese-character records and Hangeul are explicitly excluded as backward samples.
The 1500 BCE endpoint is an atlas seam and broad archaeological transition, not a fall, disappearance, invasion line, or safe successor event.
